s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic cutaneous lesions with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Asymptomatic cutaneous lesions on the face, trunk, and extremities
Monomorphic keratotic papules and symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques
key_facts: Lesions progressively spread to the trunk and extremities
Multiple millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules
Symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques on the cheeks and temples
Mild anemia with hemoglobin level of 11.3 g/dL
Positive anti-Smith, SSA/Ro, SSB/La, and anti-U1RNP antibodies

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic cutaneous lesions with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Asymptomatic cutaneous lesions on the face, trunk, and extremities
Monomorphic keratotic papules and symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques
key_facts: Lesions progressively spread to the trunk and extremities

shortlist.label: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-Smith, SSA/Ro, SSB/La, and anti-U1RNP antibodies, and characteristic skin lesions

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Raised levels of antinuclear antibodies, hypocomplementemia, and moderate proteinuria

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic skin lesions, although less likely given systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of lupus and other autoimmune features, such as raised antinuclear antibodies and positive anti-U1RNP antibodies

shortlist.label: Rowell's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Coexistence of lupus erythematosus and erythema multiforme, although less common

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules and symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques on the cheeks and temples, along with positive anti-SSA/Ro antibodies and raised levels of antinuclear antibodies, is consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus. The absence of vesicles or pustules and the specific histopathological findings also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has some systemic symptoms like asthenia and arthralgias, and laboratory findings such as mild anemia and hypocomplementemia, the primary presentation is cutaneous, suggesting a more localized form of lupus.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Discoid lupus typically presents with disc-shaped, scaly plaques, which are not described in this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: The presence of anti-U1RNP antibodies could suggest mixed connective tissue disease, but the overall clinical and laboratory picture is more consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Rowell's syndrome
rejected.why: Rowell's syndrome is a rare condition characterized by the coexistence of lupus erythematosus and erythema multiforme, which is not suggested by the patient's presentation or laboratory findings.
